summary: Iteration 9 — validated admin-login throttle, per-resident clinical thresholds, wearable threshold re-evaluation, and Haiku 4.5 memory extractor. 14/14 backend pytests passed. Frontend: all /admin-login testids present, staff-cred 403 toast + auto-redirect to /login verified, /login admin link + nurse-only demo creds verified. Admin happy-path UI redirect and Residents dialog clinical-thresholds fields could not be verified via UI because the browser's ingress IP (10.64.130.9) was exhausted by earlier test-driven failed attempts and the in-memory throttle bucket is keyed by IP+email with a 15-minute window; backend tests confirmed the underlying behavior works end-to-end.
action_items: No functional fixes required. Optional hardening: consider exempting the 'Too Many Requests' block for requests carrying a valid successful-pw path — currently a legitimate admin cannot self-unlock once locked out; they must wait 15 minutes (by design, but worth flagging to ops).

Consider keying admin throttle on request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') rather than request.client.host so multi-hop ingress traffic is throttled per real client IP rather than per internal pod IP (otherwise one aggressive client on a shared ingress can lock out innocent ones sharing the same pod-IP bucket).

Main agent: can self-verify the admin-login UI happy path + Residents dialog clinical-thresholds fields by waiting ~15 min for throttle decay, or from a new browser/IP — backend already proves persistence works.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py admin throttle is in-memory (dict on the process) — will reset on every backend restart, and won't coordinate across multiple uvicorn workers in production. Acceptable for single-worker pilot, but for 80-apartment pilot scaling, move to Redis.
wearables.py threshold logic is clean and well-commented. suppressed_event return field is a nice contract addition.
memory.py switch to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 verified live — extractor returned saved>0 and memories include valid category + importance 1-5.

Admin throttle once tripped blocks successful logins too (since throttle check runs before password verify). This is standard brute-force defense but means an attacker can intentionally lock out a legitimate admin by spamming bad passwords from the admin's IP — minor DoS risk worth noting in pilot docs.
models.py ClinicalThresholds uses extra='ignore' which is correct; but consider adding Field(ge=0) validators on the integer bands so a bogus -1 hr_max cannot be saved.

success_rate.frontend: 73% (11/15 UI assertions verified; admin-happy-path redirect + 6 clinical-threshold testids could not be reached due to IP throttle exhaustion in test env)

seed_data_creation: None — Dorothy's clinical_thresholds cleared back to null per handoff instructions. No test wearables or residents left behind (all cleaned up via fixture teardown).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The admin-login throttle is IP-keyed and in-memory. When running backend pytests + playwright in the same session, the playwright browser IP (e.g. 10.64.130.9) and curl IP (e.g. 10.64.129.166) are DIFFERENT internal pod IPs, so resetting via curl success does not unlock the browser's bucket. If the UI admin-login test returns 429, either wait 15 min for window decay or skip backend lockout tests in the same run. rca_of_the_issue: N/A — all spec items behave as designed. The only non-happy observation (UI happy-path blocked by 429 in test) is a property of IP-keyed throttling + tests draining the bucket, not a code defect.
